[Medical coding outsourcing](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/outsource-medical-coding) services can help healthcare organizations clear backlogs, cover staffing gaps, and access specialist expertise without expanding their internal coding teams.


These services follow different delivery models. Some providers supply medical coders to handle coding and audits, while others combine specialist teams with AI automation. Autonomous medical coding software offers another option for organizations seeking to automate eligible charts and reduce ongoing outsourcing dependence.


In this article, we compare 10 companies offering outsourced coding services and/or autonomous medical coding software. We examine their key features, delivery models, and suitability for different healthcare organizations to help you find the right fit for your medical coding needs.

## 1. CombineHealth


[CombineHealth](https://www.combinehealth.ai/) is a **self-learning, autonomous medical coding software that reads clinical documentation, assigns medical codes,** and **explains the reasoning behind each medical coding decision** .


CombineHealth's software can process suitable medical encounters while directing uncertain cases to human review. Healthcare **organizations retain oversight of review thresholds and coding requirements** , making CombineHealth highly suitable when the goal is to automate production while keeping control of coding operations.


### CombineHealth's Proven Results


Across deployments, CombineHealth shows proven results for:


- [98.4% medical coding accuracy](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/ai-medical-coding-accuracy-benchmarks)
- Up to 85% autonomous coding
- Up to 75% fewer coding-related denials
- Five times more CDI opportunities identified
- Up to 4% higher captured revenue


### Key Feature #1: Turns Encounter Documentation Into Medical Codes


CombineHealth reviews encounter documentation to generate diagnosis and procedure codes, evaluation and management (E/M) levels, and[modifiers](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/modifiers-in-medical-billing) . The platform supports parallel chart processing and configurable medical coding requirements.


> **Recommended Read:**[E/M Coding Guide](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/modifiers-in-medical-billing)


### Key Feature #2: Surfaces Clinical Documentation Gaps During Coding


CombineHealth checks clinical documentation while assigning medical codes, bringing[clinical documentation improvement](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/clinical-documentation-improvement-software) into its coding workflow. **It can identify missing or unclear details and flag issues requiring provider clarification.** CombineHealth’s documentation review gives medical coding teams a chance to resolve problems before affected encounters progress into billing.


### Key Feature #3: Learn From Payer Outcomes


CombineHealth applies[payer intelligence](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/payer-intelligence-ai-medical-coding) to medical coding by combining **configured payer requirements with insights from previous claim outcomes.** Denials and reimbursement patterns help identify recurring issues that may require a change in coding or validation.


Validated findings can inform future checks to help prevent recurring coding-related denials. Medical codes must remain supported by the clinical record and applicable coding guidance.


> **Recommended Read:**[How AI Helps in Preventing Medical Claim Denials](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/ai-medical-coding-denial-prevention)


### Key Feature #4: Code-Level Explainability and Auditing for Coding Quality Review


CombineHealth provides **code-level explanations** that link selected medical codes to clinical evidence and the logic applied. Medical coding reviewers can examine why a code was selected and where documentation remains insufficient.


CombineHealth can also[audit previously coded charts](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/ai-medical-coding-audit-uncovers-undercoding) . These capabilities support quality review when organizations are assessing automation alongside an existing internal or outsourced medical coding operation.


> **Recommended Read:**[Explainability in AI for Healthcare RCM](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/explainability-in-ai-for-healthcare-rcm)


> **CombineHealth Matched Expert Coders With 98%+ Accuracy Across 1,000 ED Charts**
>
>
> CombineHealth independently coded 1,000 emergency department charts alongside expert coders, achieving 85% autonomous coding, 50% faster turnaround, and identifying 5× more CDI documentation gaps.[Read the Full Case Study](https://www.combinehealth.ai/resources/customer-success-stories/case-study/ai-matched-expert-coders)


### Key Feature #5: Works Within Existing Clinical Systems


CombineHealth[integrates with electronic health record (EHR) systems](https://www.combinehealth.ai/resources/integration) such as Epic, Oracle Health (Cerner), athenahealth, and eClinicalWorks. CombineHealth reads completed encounter documentation from the EHR and sends the resulting medical codes into the existing billing workflow. This lets teams automate coding within the systems they already use.


> **CombineHealth Helped Brault Scale Autonomous Coding 5× While Maintaining 98%+ Accuracy**
>
>
> CombineHealth maintained over 98% accuracy across key coding dimensions and under 12-hour turnaround, even during 2-3× volume spikes. Brault continues production audits as it expands autonomous coding across ED sites.[Read the Full Case Study](https://www.combinehealth.ai/resources/customer-success-stories/case-study/brault-autonomous-coding)


**Best For:** Health systems and physician groups seeking autonomous medical coding with oversight of exceptions and less reliance on outsourced teams.


## 2. AGS Health


AGS Health provides outsourced facility, professional-fee, and risk-adjustment coding through certified medical coders and proprietary workflow tools. Its services cover coding production and auditing, supporting organizations that need external expertise across several coding functions.


AGS also offers an Autonomous Coding solution built around a human-in-the-loop model. AI works alongside expert medical coders, whose feedback helps refine automation. Buyers should establish which staffed services and software capabilities are included in the proposed engagement.


### Key Features


- Facility and professional-fee coding services.
- Hierarchical Condition Category (HCC) risk-adjustment coding.
- Coding audits with revenue-impact analysis.
- AI automation with medical coder feedback.


**Best For:** Hospitals seeking outsourced coding expertise alongside AI automation, with medical coders reviewing exceptions and providing feedback.


## 3. GeBBS Healthcare Solutions


GeBBS Healthcare Solutions provides outsourced medical coding and auditing through its health information management offering. Its FlexSource model lets organizations choose onshore, offshore, or mixed delivery, with coverage across inpatient, outpatient, and professional-fee coding.


GeBBS'[iCode Workflow](https://gebbs.com/technology/icode/) combines cloud-based workflow management with an autonomous coding engine and quality controls. Provider queries and custom reporting help organizations oversee outsourced production and identify where documentation clarification or additional review is needed.


### Key Features


- Configurable onshore and offshore delivery.
- Inpatient, outpatient, and professional-fee coverage.
- iCode Workflow with coding quality controls.
- Provider-query workflows and operational reporting.


**Best For:** Provider groups needing flexible coding delivery across onshore and offshore teams, with centralized workflow and quality oversight.


## 4. Solventum CodeComplete


Solventum[CodeComplete](https://www.solventum.com/en-us/home/health-information-technology/solutions/codecomplete/) Services supplies certified remote medical coders for ongoing, on-demand, or backlog support. Medical coders can work within a client's coding system, use Solventum CodeAssist, or process scanned records, depending on the organization's workflow.


Solventum's optional[CodeAssist](https://www.solventum.com/en-us/home/health-information-technology/solutions/codeassist/) system uses natural language processing to support outpatient coding and documentation review.[CodeComplete](https://www.solventum.com/en-us/home/health-information-technology/solutions/codecomplete/) also offers optional auditing and custom reports, while operational dashboards provide visibility into production and turnaround. The service combines external staffing with supporting technology.


### Key Features


- Certified remote medical coding teams.
- Multiple system-access and record-processing options.
- Optional computer-assisted coding through[CodeAssist](https://www.solventum.com/en-us/home/health-information-technology/solutions/codeassist/) .
- Operational dashboards and optional coding audits.


**Best For:** Specialty practices needing remote medical coders for staffing gaps, backlogs, or ongoing coverage within existing coding systems.


## 5. Omega Healthcare


Omega Healthcare provides managed medical coding supported by technology and specialist teams. Its published engagements include professional and facility coding, with services that can extend into broader revenue cycle operations.


Omega's middle-cycle offering connects medical records coding with documentation improvement, chart auditing, education, and charge capture. The[Omega Digital Platform](https://www.omegahms.com/omega-digital-platform/) adds automation and human workflow coordination, making the company relevant to organizations evaluating coding within a wider operational partnership.


### Key Features


- Professional and facility medical coding support.
- Documentation improvement and charge capture.
- Chart audits, coding education, and risk-adjustment reviews.
- Workflow automation and operational analytics.


**Best For:** Hospitals seeking managed medical coding within a broader partnership covering documentation improvement, chart audits, and charge capture.


## 6. Access Healthcare


Access Healthcare delivers outsourced medical coding through experienced teams supported by workflow technology. Its hospital services cover inpatient, outpatient, and emergency department coding, with local and offshore delivery options.


Access Healthcare's[arc.in](https://www.accesshealthcare.com/how/technology) platform lets clients see who is working on their accounts, the work assigned, productivity, and audit scores. Access also offers computer-assisted and autonomous coding solutions, with capabilities varying by specialty and care setting. Buyers can evaluate staffing and automation within the same provider portfolio.


### Key Features


- Hospital coding across multiple care settings.
- Workforce and audit visibility through arc.in.
- Coding-denial analysis and correction support.
- Coding audits and clinician education.


**Best For:** Hospital revenue cycle teams seeking outsourced coders with visibility into assigned work, productivity, and audit scores.


## 7. CorroHealth


CorroHealth provides outsourced medical coding through employed domestic and global teams. Its services include inpatient, professional-fee, emergency department, and risk-adjustment coding, alongside the company's[PULSE](https://corrohealth.com/pulse/) autonomous coding technology.


PULSE provides autonomous medical coding, configurable workflows, and visibility into coding decisions. Cases that fall below its confidence threshold go to medical coders for review. CorroHealth also offers coding and documentation audits, using scorecards and education to help organizations address quality problems identified during review.


### Key Features


- Employed coding teams without subcontractors.
- PULSE autonomous coding with configurable workflows.
- Facility and professional-fee coding audits.
- Documentation and coding education informed by findings.


**Best For:** Hospital coding leaders seeking outsourced production alongside documentation audits and targeted education to address recurring quality issues.


## 8. IKS Health


IKS Health offers full medical coding outsourcing, staff augmentation, and coding audits. Its approach combines autonomous coding for repeatable charts with certified medical coders who handle complex cases and lower-confidence decisions.


The service covers inpatient, outpatient, hospital, and professional-fee work. IKS links medical codes to supporting documentation and records coding rationale. Its audit offering also includes remediation plans and medical coder education, allowing organizations to address quality and staffing requirements together.


### Key Features


- Confidence-based routing to medical coders.
- Clinical evidence supporting coding decisions.
- Pre-bill and post-bill coding audits.
- Remediation plans and coder education.


**Best For:** Physician groups adding medical coders to internal teams, with options for full outsourcing and coding audits.


## 9. Infinx


Infinx combines certified medical coders with Maverick's[mCoder](https://maverick-ai.com/mcoder/) automation. Its medical coding services support professional-fee and facility workflows, with onshore and offshore delivery. Human specialists review exceptions and validate medical codes against the clinical record.


Infinx also investigates coding-related denials and reviews claims after submission. Its specialists use recurring denial patterns to recommend changes to medical coding and documentation workflows, supporting organizations that need production capacity alongside help addressing coding rework.


### Key Features


- Medical coders with specialty-specific expertise.
- Onshore and offshore coding delivery.
- Prospective, concurrent, retrospective, and focused reviews.
- Coding-denial analysis and correction or appeal support.


**Best For:** Specialty practices needing medical coding expertise alongside investigation, correction, or appeal support for recurring coding-related denials.


## 10. Advantum Health


Advantum Health provides medical coding services as part of its broader revenue cycle management offering. Its coding operation combines certified, specialty-specific medical coders with Advantum One, the company’s proprietary RCM platform.


Advantum Health also connects medical coding with downstream revenue cycle workflows.[Advantum One](https://advantumhealth.com/) pulls documented encounters from the EHR into the coding workflow, tracks encounter status and coding performance, and gives leadership visibility into coder-level accuracy. Coding findings can also be fed back to providers when documentation gaps affect code assignment.


### Key Features


- Specialty-specific medical coding across more than 35 clinical specialties
- ICD-10, CPT, HCPCS, E/M validation, and modifier application
- Documentation gap identification and provider feedback
- EHR-connected coding workflows through Advantum One
- Coding audits and coder-level performance monitoring


**Best For:** Hospitals, health systems, physician groups, ambulatory surgery centers, academic medical centers, behavioral health organizations, and specialty practices.


## How to Evaluate Medical Coding Outsourcing Services


Evaluate medical coding outsourcing services **against your actual chart mix, staffing needs, and quality standards.** Define whether the engagement should cover all coding, selected specialties, or overflow work. Then establish who handles documentation queries, automation exceptions, and corrections.


For organizations considering[broader revenue cycle outsourcing](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/outsourcing-revenue-cycle-management-healthcare) , specify the handoff between medical coding and billing so responsibility remains clear.


**Evaluation Area**


**Evidence to Check**


Coding scope


Results from representative specialties and inpatient, outpatient, or professional-fee charts.


Quality measurement


Audit methodology, sample size, error severity, and correction procedures.


Automation coverage


Share of total charts completed without intervention, plus exception ownership.


Security and integration


Data-access controls, delivery locations, system requirements, and chart-return workflows.


Total cost


Implementation, coding, audits, rework, exception handling, and retained internal effort.


> Measured against these criteria, CombineHealth reports the evidence buyers ask for: up to 85% of charts coded without intervention (automation coverage), 98.4% accuracy with a code-level audit trail for quality measurement, explainable exceptions your own coders own, and native integration with EHRs such as Epic, Oracle Health, athenahealth, and eClinicalWorks. Because it runs as software on your existing systems, the retained internal effort is review and oversight, not full re-coding.

## FAQs


### How is CombineHealth different from a medical coding outsourcing service?


CombineHealth is autonomous coding software, not a staffed outsourcing service. Instead of sending charts to an external team, it reads your clinical documentation and codes eligible encounters automatically on your own systems, directing only uncertain cases to your coders. That lets a health system add coding capacity and reduce outsourcing dependence while keeping control of review thresholds and coding operations.


### How accurate is CombineHealth's autonomous coding?


Across deployments, CombineHealth reports 98.4% coding accuracy with up to 85% of charts coded autonomously. In a head-to-head on 1,000 emergency department charts, it matched expert coders at 98%+ accuracy with 50% faster turnaround, and at Brault it sustained 98%+ accuracy across key coding dimensions through 2–3x volume spikes.


### Can CombineHealth reduce our reliance on outsourced coders?


Yes. By coding eligible encounters automatically and routing only exceptions to your team, CombineHealth lets organizations handle more volume with less outsourced capacity. Teams can start in audit mode or on a subset of charts, then expand automation as they validate accuracy — reducing reliance on external coders without losing oversight.


### What Do Medical Coding Outsourcing Services Include?


Medical coding outsourcing services use external specialists to review clinical documentation and assign medical codes. Depending on the agreement, services may also include coding audits, documentation queries, risk-adjustment coding, and coding-denial support. Confirm the contracted scope.


### Does Autonomous Coding Eliminate Human Review?


Autonomous coding can complete eligible charts without routine manual intervention. Human review remains important for uncertain cases, documentation questions, and quality oversight. Evaluate automation coverage and coding accuracy separately for your own specialties and chart mix.


Ask how uncertain records are routed, who reviews them, and whether that review is included in the service. Confirm that review outcomes remain visible to your coding leaders.


### How Should We Compare Coding Outsourcing Costs?


Compare the total cost of delivering accepted coding output. Include implementation, routine coding, quality audits, corrections, and any internal work retained. For automated services, clarify whether exception handling and specialist review are included in the quoted price.
